text.p: These are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Association of Retailers and traders (GRTU) proposes alternative tax system to VAT. The new Labour government has promised to remove Value Added Tax, introduced by the previous government in 1994. The GRTU is proposing an excise duty system, with the revenue being collected from importers and manufacturers rather than from consumers.
- Foreign Minister George Vella meets EU foreign ministers in Brussels on Monday. He is to explain Malta's policy over the EU after its decision not to continue to seek full membership.

- Minister's decision on new housing project withdrawn in propaganda exercise. The minister had picked a site for the building of a new housing estate but was forced to step back when it was realised this was fertile land.

- Previous government had planned Gozo Channel fares rise, prime minister says. Alfred Sant told a political activity that the previous government had planned but not announced it would raise fares for the ferries linking Malta with the sister island of Gozo to finance the building of new ferries.
